title: 04 — Certifications and Portfolio
html:
04 — Certifications and Portfolio

The one idea: certifications prove you studied a platform's vocabulary. A portfolio proves you can build. Use certifications as milestones along the tracks, and let projects carry the weight.

1. Databricks certifications (checked 2026-10-26)

From Databricks' published exam guides and third-party trackers. Exam versions change, so always download the current exam guide from Databricks before studying.

Certification Fits after Notes
Data Engineer Associate Data Engineer Track L2 A third-party tracker dated the current version May 2026: lakehouse, PySpark and Spark SQL, Lakeflow Jobs, Unity Catalog
Data Engineer Professional Data Engineer Track L3 Advanced pipelines, performance, governance, deployment
Data Analyst Associate Optional Databricks SQL and dashboards
Machine Learning Associate ML Engineer Track L2 ML workflow on Databricks
Machine Learning Professional ML Engineer Track L3 Production ML, MLOps
Generative AI Engineer Associate ML Engineer Track L3 Databricks' guide dated March 2026: 45 questions in 90 minutes, valid 2 years. Covers search, Model Serving, MLflow and Unity Catalog
Apache Spark Developer Associate Data Engineer Track L2 Spark DataFrame API

Third-party sources list the core exams at USD 200 each, with no formal prerequisites. Confirm on the Databricks certification site.

2. How to prepare

  1. Download the exam guide and map each objective to a note in the tracks.
  2. Do the hands-on for every objective in Free Edition. Don't just read.
  3. Take the official practice material where available. Use unofficial question dumps never: they are often wrong and break exam terms.
  4. Book the exam once you can explain every objective without notes.

3. Portfolio projects

Each project is in Git, with a README covering the problem, design, how to run it, tests, and what you'd do next. Use made-up or public data only.

Project Shows Track and level
Bronze, Silver and Gold NAV pipeline with quarantine SQL, layers, data quality DE L1
Incremental CDC to SCD2 with a backfill test Idempotency, CDC, testing DE L2
Bitemporal Iceberg table with corrections and as-of queries (capstone) Open formats, history DE L3
Bundle-deployed pipeline and jobs with dev and prod targets Platform engineering, CI/CD Databricks L2
System-tables cost and governance dashboard Operations, cost Databricks L3
Point-in-time credit model with walk-forward evaluation ML rigour ML L2
Champion and challenger with drift monitoring MLOps ML L3
Document extraction with confidence, review queue and golden-set evaluation Document AI ML L3
LoRA fine-tune vs prompted baseline on a frozen set LLM engineering ML L4

4. Questions to test yourself

  1. Why can't certifications replace a portfolio?
  2. Where do you get the current scope of an exam?
  3. Which certification fits after the data engineer's Level 2?
  4. What should every portfolio README contain?
  5. Why avoid question dumps?

Answers

  1. They test knowledge of the vocabulary and features, not the ability to build and run real systems.
  2. From the current official exam guide published by Databricks.
  3. Data Engineer Associate (and optionally Spark Developer Associate).
  4. The problem, design, how to run it, the tests, and next steps.
  5. They are often wrong, they teach nothing, and using them can break exam terms.

5. Sources
